narrative_purpose: Teaches Earth's deep thermostat as a closed loop: CO2 weathers rock, the sea buries it as carbonate, subduction cooks it, volcanoes exhale it again — and the temperature-sensitive weathering step makes the whole ring a self-correcting negative feedback.
subject: A continuous panoramic geological cross-section showing Earth's carbonate-silicate geochemical cycle. High inland mountains are weathered by rainfall from dense storm clouds; braided rivers carry dissolved ions down into a vibrant turquoise sea where marine shell organisms precipitate calcium carbonate sediments onto the seafloor; tectonic plate subduction pushes the carbonate crust deep into the Earth's mantle; active volcanic peaks melt the subducted crust and vent carbon dioxide plumes back into the atmospheric sky.
